title: Why the taker’s timeout must be shorter
summary: Bob answers with a timeout that outlasts Alice's; she claims his USD late and refunds her GBP, ending with both sides.

steps.title: Make Alice
steps.text: Every action on a blockchain is signed by a key. This creates Alice's. She will be the maker: she offers pounds and says what she wants back.

steps.title: Make Bob
steps.text: Bob gets his own key. He will be the taker: he answers Alice's offer with dollars.

steps.title: Start chain dave
steps.text: A chain is a private practice network. This swap uses two chains that know nothing about each other: dave, where the pounds will live, and sue, where the dollars will live. Alice and Bob each get some of dave's own coin to pay fees.

steps.title: Start chain sue
steps.text: The second chain. Both of them need coin here too: Alice will claim on sue, and Bob locks his dollars here.

steps.title: Alice creates pounds on dave
steps.text: A token is a made-up currency tracked by a program on one chain. Alice creates pounds (GBP, two decimal places) on dave and receives all one million of them.

steps.title: Bob creates dollars on sue
steps.text: Bob creates dollars (USD, six decimal places) on sue and receives all one million. Pounds exist only on dave, dollars only on sue: no single program can see both.

steps.title: Put a HashLock on dave
steps.text: Since no program sees both chains, each chain gets its own HashLock: a program that holds tokens until someone shows a secret, or hands them back to the sender after a deadline. Alice puts one on dave.

steps.title: Put a HashLock on sue
steps.text: Bob puts the same program on sue. Anyone could have done it; one per chain is enough for every swap.

steps.title: Alice allows dave's HashLock to move her pounds
steps.text: Before a program can move your tokens you must say it may, and how many. Alice allows the HashLock on dave to take the 1,000 pounds she will lock.

steps.title: Alice locks 1,000 pounds on dave for Bob
steps.text: Her browser makes a secret: 32 random bytes only she knows, kept in this browser. The lock carries only its hash, a fingerprint anyone can check a secret against but nobody can turn back into the secret. Bob can take the pounds by showing the secret within 100 of dave's blocks; after that only Alice can take them back. The lock also states her terms: 1,270 dollars on sue.

steps.title: Bob allows sue's HashLock to move his dollars
steps.text: Bob will answer on sue, so he allows the HashLock there to take the 1,270 dollars Alice asked for.

steps.title: Bob locks with a timeout that is too long
steps.text: This time Bob gives his lock 95 of sue's blocks, while Alice's has 99 left on dave. The page warns him: his lock should end at least 10 blocks before hers, because Alice claims first and could wait until hers expires. Bob presses Lock anyway.

steps.title: Time passes on dave
steps.text: Practice chains only make blocks when transactions arrive, so Advance blocks stands in for time passing. dave makes 100 blocks: Alice's lock has timed out, so from now on nobody can claim the pounds, not even Bob with the secret.

steps.title: The same time passes on sue
steps.text: sue makes 90 blocks. Bob's lock had 95, so it is still open, and Alice still knows the secret.

steps.title: Alice claims the dollars late
steps.text: Alice shows her secret on sue and takes Bob's 1,270 dollars. Bob can now read the secret, but on dave it is too late: Alice's lock there has timed out.

steps.title: Alice takes her pounds back too
steps.text: The HashLock on dave returns the pounds to Alice, so she ends with both sides and Bob with nothing. The report flags unsafe timeouts: this is why the taker's timeout must end well before the maker's, and why the page asks Bob to confirm.
